# Code review: the change that makes relayer choice come from the config service

**Mode:** committed range `e88f197…HEAD` (base at merge-base `7b8dd82`, head `e6b01d9`). This was a full review with the two top findings checked independently. Following your limits, I used only 2 agents and ran all nine review passes myself.
25 files, +476 −380 · 5 repo rules (AGENTS.md: layering, updating specs, pre-commit, license headers, datasource per API) · 9 of 9 areas have surface

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Don't open yet.** Two confirmed P1s would turn relaying into 500s or 403s on chains that work today. |
| **Score** | **82 / 100**. Capped by the P1 gate. Checked independently: 2 of 6 findings (both confirmed by the checking agent, neither overturned by the arguing agent). |
| **What held it down** | Correctness (1 P1), regression (1 P1), testing (1 P2) |
| **Fix first** | #1: guard the missing no-fee-campaign config, or refuse to route to it |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bugs | 70 | #1 |
| Regression | 70 | #2 |
| Testing | 85 | #3 |
| Architecture | 95 | #5 |
| Conventions | 95 | #6 |
| Security | 100 | Checked the 403 body contents, what reaches the new error message, and the filter wiring. Nothing found. |
| Performance | 100 | The new `getChain` call on the relay and fee-preview paths goes through the cached config API. Nothing found. |
| DRY | 100 | The new filter repeats `RelayDeniedExceptionFilter` on purpose, following the repo's pattern. |
| KISS | 100 | Nothing found. |

## Not covered
- **Production config data.** I can't see whether the config service already returns `relayerType` for every chain. That decides how bad #2 is.
- **No tests or app run** (as you asked). Findings come from reading code and `git show` of the base.
- **Last-run tracking skipped.** I didn't write `.git/safe-code-review/last-run.tsv` because you asked for no files to be created, so there's no "since your last run" section.
- **Adjudication limited by the 2-agent cap.** Only #1 and #2 were checked, one agent confirming and one arguing against both. #3–#6 are unchecked and count at full weight.

## Fix before opening

**#1 · P1 · Bugs · Confirmed (validator 45, refuter found no guard)**
`src/modules/relay/domain/relayers/no-fee-campaign.relayer.ts:81-83`, reached from `src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:55`
- **What happens:** `getRelayer` now picks `NoFeeCampaignRelayer` whenever the config service says `NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN`. The old code also required a local `relay.noFeeCampaign[chainId]` entry, and this change removes that check.
- **Why it breaks:** `relay()` then reads `this.relayConfiguration[chainId].maxGasLimit` with no guard. Its sibling methods (`canRelay` :46, `getRelaysRemaining` :134) do have the guard. Locally, the config only defines chains `1` and `11155111` (`src/config/entities/configuration.ts:653-695`).
- **Result:** if any other chain is flagged `NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN` in the config service, `POST /v1/chains/:id/relay` throws a `TypeError` and returns **500**. Nothing upstream stops it: `LimitAddressesMapper` never touches this config, and the controller filters only catch typed errors.
- **Fix:** in the `NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN` branch, throw `NoRelayerDefinedError` (or a clearer error) when there's no local config. Or add the missing guard in `relay()`. Add a manager/relayer test for this mismatch.

**#2 · P1 · Regression · Confirmed (validator 50, refuter found no fallback)**
`src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:59-60`, `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:108`
- **What happens:** before, any chain that wasn't configured fell back to `DailyLimitRelayer`, with an explicit backward-compatibility comment. Now, a `null` relayer type throws `NoRelayerDefinedError` and returns **403**. That covers a missing field, and also any unknown value, because `.catch(null)` turns it into `null`.
- **Which endpoints:** both `POST relay` and `GET relays-remaining` (`relay.repository.ts:27,45`).
- **Why it matters:** `.env.sample.json:1161` defaulted `RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS` to Sepolia only. So most chains that relay today do it through the fallback you removed.
- **Result:** if this deploys before the config service sets `relayerType` on every chain, relaying on those chains starts returning 403 immediately.
- **Fix:** pick one before merging:
  - get the config service backfilled and verified first, and say so in the PR, or
  - keep a temporary `DAILY_LIMIT` fallback for `null`, with a log line.

## Worth a ticket / fix in this PR

| # | P | Area | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | P2 | Testing | `src/modules/relay/routes/relay.controller.ts:82,156` | The new 403 path isn't tested end to end. No integration test covers `null` or `GTF` on POST relay or GET relays-remaining, so the filter wiring and response body are unchecked. No controller test covers `RELAY_FEE` routing either. If `RelayerNotAvailableExceptionFilter` is dropped from either `@UseFilters`, every test still passes. |
| 4 | P3 | Bugs | `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:108` | `.catch(null)` silently turns an unknown relayer type from the config service (such as a new value) into "No relayer defined", with no log. That makes a misconfiguration look like a deliberate block. Log the swallowed value. |
| 5 | P3 | Architecture | `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:6` | The shared `chains` domain schema now imports from `modules/relay`, while `relay` and `fees` already import `ChainsModule`. There's no runtime cycle (the entity has no imports), but the dependency goes both ways. The `RelayerType` enum belongs with the chain entity or in a shared domain location. |
| 6 | P3 | Conventions | `.env.sample.json:1161-1172` | The file still documents the removed `RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS` (as `required: true`) and `RELAY_FEE_CHAIN_IDS`. `yarn env:validate` will warn about both as extra variables. |

## Your call

| # | Choice |
|---|---|
| 1 | fix now (small guard + test) |
| 2 | decide the rollout: backfill first, or a temporary fallback |
| 3 | fix now: add two integration cases (null → 403 on POST and GET) |
| 4–6 | fix now; each is a few lines |

## Worth tidying (optional, no score impact)
- `relay.controller.ts`: the relay endpoints have no `@ApiForbiddenResponse`, though 403 is now a documented outcome. `RelayDenied` has the same gap, and it predates this change.
- `relay.manager.ts:6-9`: `RelayerType` is imported twice, once as a value and once as a type alias (`RelayerTypeValue`). `relay-manager.interface.ts` imports it once. A single import works here too, since the name serves as both value and type.

## Checked and nothing found
License headers on all 25 changed files (all present). No new chain field leaks into the public chains API: the route entity maps fields explicitly. Every `chainBuilder()` in the relay integration spec sets `relayerType`, so the builder's random `null`/`GTF` can't cause flaky tests there.

**Ruled out:** nothing. **Not checked independently:** #3–#6.

## How this was produced
The whole pipeline ran in this session except checking: scope → profile → nine passes → checking → score → report. Two agents checked #1 and #2, one confirming and one arguing against, instead of the usual pair per finding. Nothing was modified, installed, run as tests, or posted.
